charters.name: Liberal Arts College
charters.blurb: Small classes, a great books seminar and a chapel bell. The founders believed a college should make people, not careers.

charters.name: Research University
charters.blurb: Laboratories before lawns. The founders wanted discoveries, and they expected the undergraduates to keep up.

charters.name: Polytechnic
charters.blurb: Workshops, drawing offices and a motto about useful knowledge. The founders built bridges and wanted more people who could.

charters.name: Land-Grant College
charters.blurb: Founded on a public mission, with a farm, a football team and a promise that anyone who could do the work would be let in.

words.title: The founding charter
words.hint: What the founders meant the college to be. It sets which school is cheaper to found, which capital project and grand landmark come at a discount, where the standings lean in the first decades, and the questions the world tends to ask. It is a college's first identity, not its last: the lean fades by Year 25.
